# FleetKit Control Plane (`.fleet/`) — ConversationKit

Welcome to the **FleetKit Control Plane** for **ConversationKit**.

`.fleet/` is the **single source of truth** for this repository's hierarchical AI coding fleet. Instead of maintaining fragmented, tool-specific configuration files across the repository, you declare your spatial architecture, folder ownership, specialist agents, declarative skills, project rules, and operational workflows once inside `.fleet/`. FleetKit then compiles and projects them into native configurations for every supported AI coding harness.

---

## 🗂️ Directory & File Structure

```text
.fleet/
├── fleet.yaml                          # Root control plane manifest & spatial routing rules
├── FLEET.md                            # Compiled FleetKit workspace directives (auto-generated on 'fleetkit sync')
├── README.md                           # This guide (auto-generated on 'fleetkit sync')
├── agents/                             # Specialist & orchestrator agent definitions (*.md)
├── skills/                             # Declarative skill manifests (*.md)
├── rules/                              # Project-wide architectural & coding rules (*.md)
├── workflows/                          # Multi-stage operational workflow playbooks (*.md)
├── templates/                          # Markdown templates for PRDs, ADRs, Journals & Learnings
├── tools/                              # Optional custom CLI tool definitions & fallback chains
├── hooks/                              # Auto-generated runtime gatekeeper scripts
├── worktrees/                          # Ephemeral isolated Git worktrees (git-ignored)
└── cache/                              # Ephemeral local resolution cache (git-ignored)
```

### User-Editable vs. Auto-Generated Files

| Path | Ownership | Role & Responsibility |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `fleet.yaml` | **User-Editable** | Root manifest defining project metadata, master orchestrator, feature flags, tool allowlists, spatial `hierarchy` routes, and `shared` docs paths. |
| `agents/*.md` | **User-Editable** | Agent system prompts with YAML frontmatter (`id`, `name`, `role`, `description`). Customize existing specialists or add new custom agents here. |
| `skills/*.md` | **User-Editable** | Declarative skill manifests (`id`, `name`, `repository`, `path`, `branch`, plus offline fallback content). Resolved into `.agents/skills/<id>/SKILL.md`. |
| `rules/*.md` | **User-Editable** | Project-specific architectural, concurrency, or security rules. Automatically inlined into workspace directives (`.fleet/FLEET.md`, `.agents/rules/fleetkit.md`, `.claude/rules/fleetkit.md`) and subagent definitions. |
| `workflows/*.md` | **User-Editable** | Playbooks for `/fix`, `/feature`, `/spec`, `/challenge`, and `/audit` workflows. |
| `templates/*.md` | **User-Editable** | Document templates (`PRD_TEMPLATE.md`, `ADR_TEMPLATE.md`, `JOURNAL_TEMPLATE.md`, `LEARNING_TEMPLATE.md`) used by lifecycle specialists. |
| `tools/*.md` | **User-Editable** *(Optional)* | Custom CLI tool definitions and sequential fallback chains (`id`, `binary`, `fallback`). |
| `FLEET.md` | **Auto-Generated** | Canonical compiled root orchestrator directives, spatial routing table, and project rules reference in `.fleet/`. |
| `hooks/*.mjs` | **Auto-Generated** | Runtime gatekeeper scripts (`antigravity-fleet-gate.mjs`) enforcing orchestrator edit boundaries and subagent dispatch protocols. |
| `worktrees/` | **Ephemeral** *(Git-Ignored)* | Isolated Git worktrees created during parallel multi-surface subagent execution to prevent working-copy conflicts. |
| `cache/` | **Ephemeral** *(Git-Ignored)* | Local working cache for skill and template resolution. |
| `README.md` | **Auto-Generated** | This documentation file, kept in sync automatically by `fleetkit sync`. |

## 🔍 Detailed Role of Each Component

### 1. `fleet.yaml` (Root Manifest & Spatial Routing)
`fleet.yaml` is the heart of the control plane. It configures:
- **`orchestrator`**: Designates the primary non-coding orchestrator (`agents/chief-of-staff.md`) and routing strategy (`hierarchical`).
- **`features`**: Toggles lifecycle capabilities including `critics` (Council of Critics plan review), `adversarial-qa` (`/challenge` Red Team stress testing), `human-in-the-loop` (user approval gates), `reconciler` (automatic structural drift detection), and `firebase`.
- **`tools`**: Declares active developer CLI tools (e.g., `flowdeck`, `rocketsim`, `firebase`) and their deterministic fallback chains.
- **`default`**: Fallback lead owner, reviewers, and verification command when a file path does not match a specific hierarchy rule.
- **`hierarchy`**: Ordered spatial routing rules mapping glob patterns (such as `frontend/apple/**` or `backend/api/**`) to a Domain Pack (`pack`), lead engineer (`owners.lead`), peer reviewers (`owners.reviewers`), domain `skills`, `rules`, and localized `verification` commands (`build`, `test`).
- **`shared`**: Canonical paths for cross-cutting project knowledge (`docs/`, `docs/specs/`, `docs/architecture/`).
- **Subtree Overrides (`.fleet.yaml`)**: Any subdirectory in the repository can also include a local `.fleet.yaml` file to override the lead agent, skills, or verification command for that specific subtree using `.gitignore`-style closest-ancestor cascading resolution.

### 2. `agents/` (Orchestrator, Surface Leads & Lifecycle Specialists)
Markdown files in `.fleet/agents/` define the personas, architectural boundaries, and verification mandates for every agent in the fleet:
- **Master Orchestrator**: `chief-of-staff.md` — Triages requests, inspects spatial routing, and dispatches tasks to domain specialists without making direct monolithic code edits.
- **Lifecycle Specialists**:
  - `product-manager.md` — Authors PRDs and user stories in `docs/specs/`.
  - `senior-architect.md` — Designs system blueprints and ADRs in `docs/architecture/`.
  - `code-reviewer.md` — Performs read-only static analysis, concurrency checks, and diff reviews.
  - `adversarial-tester.md` — Probes boundary conditions, audits PRD acceptance criteria, and writes exploit tests during `/challenge`.
  - `journal-agent.md` & `learnings-agent.md` — Maintain engineering journals (`docs/journal/`) and reusable technical discoveries (`docs/learnings/`).
- **Domain Surface Leads**: Platform specialists installed from Domain Packs (such as `apple-engineer.md`, `swift-sdk-architect.md`, `android-engineer.md`, `web-engineer.md`, `cli-engineer.md`, `mcp-architect.md`, `firebase-architect.md`, etc.) or custom agents added by your team.

### 3. `skills/` (Declarative Skill Manifests)
Each `.md` file in `.fleet/skills/` is a lightweight manifest declaring a domain skill via YAML frontmatter (`id`, `name`, `description`, and optional upstream `repository`, `path`, `branch`) along with embedded offline fallback instructions.
During `fleetkit sync`, `fleetkit init`, or `fleetkit update`, the **Skill Resolver** fetches upstream skill repositories (caching them in `~/.fleet/cache/skills/`) or uses the embedded fallback, and materializes full skill bundles into `.agents/skills/<skill-id>/SKILL.md`.

### 4. `rules/` (Project-Specific Rules)
Drop any Markdown file (`*.md`) into `.fleet/rules/` (with an optional `title` in YAML frontmatter) to enforce repo-wide architectural, concurrency, or security constraints. When `fleetkit sync` runs, every rule in `.fleet/rules/` is automatically:
1. Inlined into the **Active Project Rules** section of `.fleet/FLEET.md`, `.agents/rules/fleetkit.md`, and `.claude/rules/fleetkit.md` (avoiding duplicate per-file rule injection into `.agents/rules/`).
2. Composed into subagent system prompts via the runtime gatekeeper hook.

### 5. `workflows/` & `templates/` (Engineering Pipelines & Artifacts)
- **`workflows/`**: Contains the canonical operational playbooks (`fix.md`, `feature.md`, `spec.md`, `challenge.md`, `audit.md`). These use target-agnostic macro placeholders (like `{{fragment:subagent-delegation}}` and `{{fragment:verification-mandate}}`) that expand into harness-native instructions during projection.
- **`templates/`**: Standardized Markdown templates (`PRD_TEMPLATE.md`, `ADR_TEMPLATE.md`, `JOURNAL_TEMPLATE.md`, `LEARNING_TEMPLATE.md`) referenced by lifecycle agents so project documentation remains consistent.

## ⚙️ How Everything Is Assembled (Compilation & Projection Pipeline)

When you run `fleetkit sync` (or `fleetkit init`, `fleetkit update`, `fleetkit reconcile`), FleetKit executes a deterministic 4-stage compilation pipeline:

```text
                    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
                    │         .fleet/ Control Plane           │
                    │  fleet.yaml • agents/*.md • skills/*.md │
                    │  rules/*.md • workflows/*.md • tools/   │
                    └────────────────────┬────────────────────┘
                                         │
              + Subtree .fleet.yaml      │      + Bundled Domain Packs
                Overrides                ▼        (@fleetkit/core, etc.)
                    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
                    │   FleetKit Compiler & Projector Engine  │
                    │  1. Hierarchy & Cascading Resolution    │
                    │  2. Macro Fragment & Rule Composition   │
                    │  3. Tool Fallback Chain Resolution      │
                    │  4. Declarative Skill Materialization   │
                    └─┬────────────┬────────────┬───────────┬─┘
                      │            │            │           │
        ┌─────────────┘            │            │           └─────────────┐
        ▼                          ▼            ▼                         ▼
┌───────────────┐        ┌───────────────┐  ┌──────────────────┐  ┌───────────────┐
│  Antigravity  │        │  Claude Code  │  │     OpenCode     │  │    Cursor     │
├───────────────┤        ├───────────────┤  ├──────────────────┤  ├───────────────┤
│ • .agents/    │        │ • .claude/    │  │ • .fleet/        │  │ • .cursorrules│
│   rules/      │        │   rules/      │  │   FLEET.md       │  │ • .cursor/    │
│   fleetkit.md │        │   fleetkit.md │  │ • .opencode/     │  │   rules/*.mdc │
│ • .agents/    │        │ • .claude/    │  │   opencode.jsonc │  │               │
│   hooks.json  │        │   agents/*.md │  │ • .opencode/     │  │               │
│ • .agents/    │        │ • .claude/    │  │   agents/*.md    │  │               │
│   skills/     │        │   commands/   │  │ • .opencode/     │  │               │
│               │        │   *.md        │  │   commands/*.md  │  │               │
└───────────────┘        └───────────────┘  └──────────────────┘  └───────────────┘
```

### Stage 1: Configuration & Hierarchy Resolution
FleetKit parses `.fleet/fleet.yaml` and discovers any nested `.fleet.yaml` subtree overrides across the workspace. It merges them with the active Domain Packs (`@fleetkit/core`, `@fleetkit/apple-app`, `@fleetkit/web-modern`, `@fleetkit/backend`, etc.) to compute the spatial routing table, active feature gates, and localized verification commands.

### Stage 2: Prompt Fragment Composition & Rule Inlining
Agent definitions (`.fleet/agents/*.md`) and workflow playbooks (`.fleet/workflows/*.md`) are compiled through the Fragment Composer:
- Target-specific macro fragments (`{{fragment:subagent-delegation}}`, `{{fragment:verification-mandate}}`) are expanded for each target harness.
- Project rules from `.fleet/rules/*.md` are inlined into root orchestrator directives.
- Active CLI tools and their sequential fallback chains (e.g., `flowdeck` ➔ `xcbeautify` / `xcodebuild`) are injected into agent tooling sections.

### Stage 3: Declarative Skill Materialization
The Skill Resolver reads every manifest in `.fleet/skills/*.md`, resolves upstream content (or offline fallbacks), and writes normalized skill bundles to `.agents/skills/<skill-id>/SKILL.md` so agents can load specialized domain knowledge on demand.

### Stage 4: Multi-Harness Projection
Finally, FleetKit emits native configuration artifacts tailored to each coding harness (skipping unmodified files via SHA-256 preflight checks and leaving root `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` untouched for user/agent customization):

- **Antigravity**:
  - `.agents/rules/fleetkit.md`: Always-on rule file (`trigger: always_on`) containing root orchestrator directives, spatial routing table, lifecycle routing, inlined project rules, and the deterministic Subagent Dispatch Protocol.
  - `.agents/hooks.json` & `.fleet/hooks/antigravity-fleet-gate.mjs`: PreToolUse and Stop gatekeeper hooks that enforce orchestrator non-coding boundaries and automatic subagent prompt composition.
  - `.agents/skills/<id>/SKILL.md`: Materialized declarative project skills.
- **Claude Code**:
  - `.claude/settings.json`: Sets `chief-of-staff` as the default primary agent (`{ "agent": "chief-of-staff" }`).
  - `.claude/rules/fleetkit.md`: Auto-loaded rule file containing root orchestrator directives, spatial routing table, lifecycle specialist routing, and active project rules.
  - `.claude/agents/*.md`: Compiled primary and subagent definitions (with read-only `disallowedTools` guardrails on `chief-of-staff` and `code-reviewer`) loaded automatically by Claude Code and the `Agent` tool.
  - `.claude/commands/*.md`: Native slash commands (`/fix`, `/feature`, `/spec`, `/challenge`, `/audit`).
- **OpenCode / OpenChamber**:
  - `.opencode/opencode.jsonc`: Sets `chief-of-staff` as the default primary agent with edit-deny guardrails, disables generic built-in `build`/`plan` agents, configures isolated worktrees under `.fleet/worktrees`, and registers the materialized skill directory (`.agents/skills`).
  - `.opencode/agents/*.md`: Compiled primary and subagent definitions (`.opencode/agents/chief-of-staff.md` embeds the compiled FleetKit directives directly as the primary agent's system prompt, while `.fleet/FLEET.md` serves as the canonical compiled directives reference in `.fleet/`).
  - `.opencode/commands/*.md`: Native slash commands routed through `chief-of-staff`.
- **Cursor**:
  - `.cursorrules`: Root folder ownership and verification summary.
  - `.cursor/rules/<surface>.mdc`: Granular, glob-scoped rule files that automatically attach the right lead specialist, domain skills, and verification test command when editing matching files.

## 🛠️ Common FleetKit CLI Commands

| Command | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `fleetkit sync` | Recompile `.fleet/` and synchronize all harness projections and declarative skills (`--force` to overwrite). |
| `fleetkit inspect <path>` | Inspect the resolved lead agent, pack, skills, inheritance chain, and verification command for any file or folder. |
| `fleetkit graph` | Render a visual ASCII tree of the repository's spatial hierarchy and agent ownership. |
| `fleetkit reconcile` | Detect moved, added, or removed project surfaces and automatically update `.fleet/fleet.yaml` routes. |
| `fleetkit update` | Refresh pack-provided agents and skills in `.fleet/` while preserving custom agents, skills, and rules. |
| `fleetkit doctor` | Run environment diagnostics and verify required CLI tools and fallbacks for active surfaces. |
